args.text:
Batch: 8 runs, 8 accepted, 0 flagged, 8 cleared (r01–r08).
Checks: rigid invariance and closure passed on every run. Plane sections was not run on any run because every run used the width-free ratio. Its values (3.72–3.86 vs 3.25 %/h) are what you expect when root width changes.
r02, r03, r04, r06, r07, r08: every summary is within 0.15 %/h of the batch median (centre REGR peak 53.1 %/h at 421 µm, growth zone 695 µm, flank difference about -3.8 %/h at 1074 µm). Their larger |z| values come from the very small batch MAD. The single roll-backs in r03 and r08 still ended with passing checks.
r01: centre REGR peak 111.48 %/h and flank difference -7.97 %/h, both about 2.1x the batch. Its profile has the same shape as r05's (peak at 421 µm, growth zone 684 µm), it uses stride 1, and its checks pass, so it was cleared as a faster-growing root.
Worth a second look: r01 and r05 have their largest flank difference at 284 µm, while the other six have it at 1074 µm. r01's width-free ratio is also -0.268, against a median of 0.027. I judged these within tolerance, so I flagged nothing, but this curvature-rate pattern in r01 and r05 is the place to look again if the batch is re-examined.
